title: Mashomuck
summary: Mashomuck is a Shelter Island placename for the southern neck and point opposite Sag Harbor, now associated with Mashomack Preserve. Recorded forms include Meshomac, Marshammock, Mashomuk, Mashomuck, and the local pronunciation Mashom-uk.
map_geometry_source: Approximate southern Mashomack/Mashomuck neck-and-point marker based on Tooker description and modern preserve geography.
history_content: The name is described as traditional, preserved in local speech, island histories, and older geographical materials rather than as a deeply attested early legal form. The point's position made it a practical canoe-crossing landscape between Shelter Island, Sag Harbor, Gardiners Island, Three Mile Harbor, and Shinnecock routes.
translation_content:
The name is interpreted as a place where people go by boat, fitting the crossing-place geography. An earlier stockade-place interpretation was later rejected, and that correction should remain visible because the older interpretation shaped later local lore.

Why Place Names Matter

“The power to name geographical places is elemental to how human beings make and remake places, and maintain or sever relationships to places and their stories.”

— Zoltan Grossman, Decolonizing Place Names (2024), program description, opening sentence
whereintheworld_content: This blue marker is an approximate general-location point for the southern Mashomack/Mashomuck neck and point on Shelter Island. It is not an exact historic crossing, trail, village, or map coordinate.
